narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: In a hymn that Budge attributes to the Papyrus of Hunefer, the speaker says, 'I am Thoth, the perfect scribe.' Budge's separate introductory chapter reports a belief that Thoth invented writing.

narrativeBlocks.title: A ritual speaker identifies with Thoth
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Budge translation; whitespace normalized): “I have not committed any kind of sin in the land; I have defrauded no man of what is his. I am Thoth, the perfect scribe, whose hands are pure. I am the lord of purity, the destroyer of evil, the scribe of truth; what I abominate is sin.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: The words 'I am Thoth' occur in a funerary hymn's first-person declaration. They are not a biography of the god or proof that Thoth literally authored this manuscript.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read the evidence carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Budge's Chapter I is modern editorial prose; the Hunefer hymn is a translated ancient text. Keep those evidence types and voices separate.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Ask who is speaking before treating a divine identity formula as a literal statement about authorship.
